question: What was the previous term used for Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs)?
explanation: Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) were formerly referred to as nosocomial infections, which specifically meant infections acquired within a hospital environment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h1)

question: What is identified as the primary goal of the Hospital Infection Control Unit?

options.A: To increase hospital revenue through strict cleanliness
options.B: To minimize and prevent the transmission of infectious agents
options.C: To diagnose and treat chronic community illnesses
options.D: To manage the administrative duties of the nursing ward

explanation: The primary goal of the Infection Control Unit is to minimize and prevent the transmission of infectious agents among patients, staff, and visitors. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h1)

question: Who typically drives the day-to-day operational activities and surveillance within the Infection Control Unit?
explanation: The day-to-day operational activities, surveillance, and staff liaison are heavily driven by the Infection Control Nurse or Infection Control Practitioner. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h2)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for the Infection Control Unit?

options.A: Because infection control cuts across every hospital department
options.B: To reduce the workload of the medical doctors exclusively
options.C: To manage the financial budget of the hospital pharmacy
options.D: To replace the need for nursing administration

explanation: A multidisciplinary makeup is critical because infection control cuts across every department, from clinical wards to waste disposal units. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h2)

question: What characterizes active surveillance in hospital infection control?

options.A: Waiting for ward staff to report infections manually
options.B: Proactively reviewing laboratory reports, charts, and antibiotic usage
options.C: Conducting annual physical exams on all discharged patients
options.D: Restricting visitors from entering high-risk wards

explanation: Active surveillance involves trained personnel proactively reviewing laboratory reports, patient charts, and antibiotic usage to detect HAIs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h3)

question: Which of the following is a common target for hospital infection surveillance?
explanation: Common targets for surveillance include surgical site infections (SSIs), catheter-associated urinary tract infections, and ventilator-associated pneumonia. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h3)

question: What should hospital infection control policies be based upon?

options.B: Evidence-based standards adapted for local implementation
options.C: Strictly international guidelines without local modifications
options.D: Preferences of individual patients admitted to the ward

explanation: Policies must be rooted in evidence-based international standards while remaining practical and adaptable for local implementation within the facility. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h4)

question: How does the Infection Control Unit ensure compliance after developing policies?

options.A: By penalizing staff publicly for minor errors
options.B: By monitoring adherence through regular audits and feedback sessions
options.C: By delegating all enforcement duties to external security agencies
options.D: By keeping the policies confidential from bedside nurses

explanation: Once policies are developed, the unit ensures dissemination and monitors adherence through regular audits and feedback sessions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h4)

question: To whom do Standard Precautions apply in the healthcare setting?

options.A: Only to patients with confirmed infectious diseases
options.B: To the care of all patients regardless of their infection status
options.C: Exclusively to patients admitted in surgical and medical wards
options.D: Only to healthcare workers handling hazardous chemical waste

explanation: Standard Precautions are the foundational infection prevention practices applied to the care of all patients regardless of their suspected or confirmed infection status. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h5)

question: Which of the following is included under Standard Precautions?

options.A: Prohibiting all visitors from entering the hospital premises
options.B: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to every new admission
options.C: Hand hygiene and appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
options.D: Mandatory quarantine of healthcare workers after every shift

explanation: Standard Precautions include hand hygiene, appropriate use of PPE, respiratory hygiene, safe injection practices, and proper equipment handling. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h5)

question: How is an outbreak defined in the context of hospital infection control?

options.A: A single case of a rare tropical disease in the facility
options.B: An excess of infections above the expected baseline for a specific time and place
options.C: Any hospital admission that requires intensive care management
options.D: The normal seasonal fluctuation of common viral colds

explanation: An outbreak is defined as an excess of infections above the expected baseline for a specific time and place within the hospital environment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h6)

question: What is one of the immediate control measures instituted during a hospital outbreak?

options.A: Closing down the entire hospital permanently
options.B: Cohorting infected patients and reinforcing hand hygiene
options.C: Discharging all nurses to prevent further exposure
options.D: Halting all laboratory testing until further notice

explanation: Immediate control measures include cohorting infected patients, reinforcing hand hygiene, restricting ward admissions, or treating colonized staff. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h6)

question: What is a primary danger of improper waste segregation in healthcare settings?

options.A: Increased financial profit for the hospital administration
options.B: Severe occupational hazards such as needle-stick injuries
options.D: Reduction in the number of hospitalized patients

explanation: Improper waste segregation, such as mixing used needles with general trash, poses severe occupational hazards like needle-stick injuries and contamination. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h7)

question: Which color-coding convention is commonly utilized for infectious healthcare waste?
explanation: Color-coded bin systems typically use yellow for infectious waste, brown for hazardous, and black for general domestic waste. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h7)

question: Why is the timely reporting of communicable diseases to public health agencies essential?

options.B: For community disease surveillance and national epidemiological tracking
options.C: To justify purchasing more expensive pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: To determine the annual leave schedule for nursing staff

explanation: Timely reporting of communicable diseases is essential for community disease surveillance and national epidemiological tracking of infectious threats. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h8)

question: What role do nurse champions play in hospital infection control?

options.A: They audit hospital financial accounts and budgets
options.B: They advocate for policies on wards, mentor staff, and report challenges
options.C: They replace the medical laboratory scientists in testing samples
options.D: They formulate national public health laws

explanation: Nurse champions play a vital role by advocating for infection control policies on the wards, mentoring junior staff, and reporting operational challenges. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h8)
